config.title: useLocalStorage

intro.title: useLocalStorage
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a custom React hook called `useLocalStorage` that lets you store and retrieve data in the browser's local storage. You will learn how to create a reusable hook that synchronizes a state variable with local storage, so your data persists even after refreshing the page. The core concepts involve using React's `useState` and `useEffect` hooks, along with TypeScript for type safety. By the end, you'll have a practical hook you can use in any React project to manage persistent user data like theme preferences or form inputs.
intro.usecase: The useLocalStorage hook is essential for creating persistent user experiences across browser sessions. In e-commerce sites, it maintains shopping cart items when users navigate away or close tabs. Dashboard applications use it to remember user preferences like chart settings, theme choices, or collapsed/expanded panel states. Form-heavy applications benefit by saving draft inputs, preventing data loss during accidental refreshes or navigation.

objectives: Implement a custom React hook that reads and writes data to localStorage
Apply TypeScript generics to create a type-safe useLocalStorage hook
Initialize state within the hook that synchronizes with localStorage values
Construct a setter function that updates both state and localStorage
Integrate the useLocalStorage hook into a functional component to manage persistent data
Manipulate the hook to handle edge cases, such as JSON parsing errors or missing keys
Render component UI that reflects and controls the persisted state from localStorage

steps.instruction: Add a generic type parameter <T> to the useLocalStorage function signature to make it type-safe.
steps.hint: After the function name, add angle brackets with a generic type parameter like <T>. This will allow the hook to work with different types while maintaining type safety.

steps.title: Implement localStorage retrieval logic
steps.instruction: Inside the useLocalStorage function, add a function called getStoredValue that reads from localStorage and returns the stored value, or returns the initialValue if nothing is stored.
steps.hint: Use localStorage.getItem with the key parameter, then parse the stored string with JSON.parse. If the stored item is null, return the initialValue.
steps.expectedOutcome: The useLocalStorage hook now includes a helper function that can retrieve stored values from localStorage.
successCriteria: The getStoredValue function is defined inside useLocalStorage, reads from localStorage, parses the stored value, and returns either the parsed value or the initialValue.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure getStoredValue properly handles both cases: when localStorage has a value (parse it) and when it doesn't (return initialValue).
steps.feedbackWrong: The getStoredValue function isn't implemented correctly. It should read from localStorage, parse the value if it exists, or return the initialValue if nothing is stored.

steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.

steps.title: Add input field for user input
steps.instruction: Inside the App component's return statement, add an input element with its value bound to the value returned by your useLocalStorage hook and an onChange handler that calls the setter function from the hook.
steps.hint: Use the value and setter you destructured from useLocalStorage. The input should have type='text' and appropriate attributes to make it controlled.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component will render a text input field that displays the current value from localStorage and updates it when the user types.
successCriteria: The input element has value={value} and onChange={(e) => setValue(e.target.value)} attributes, where value and setValue come from useLocalStorage.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added an input, but check that it's properly controlled. Make sure it has both value and onChange attributes connected to your hook's state and setter.
steps.feedbackWrong: The input element is missing or not properly connected to the useLocalStorage hook. Ensure you're using the value and setter from the hook to create a controlled input.

successCriteria: The input element includes an onChange prop that calls the setter function from useLocalStorage with e.target.value.
